chunks: Egypt has been conquered, and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, has been martyred. We seek his reward from Allah. He was a son who was a well-wisher, a hard worker, a sharp sword and a bastion of defence.

I had roused the people to join him and ordered them to reach him to help before this incident. I called to them secretly as well as openly repeatedly. Some of them came half-heartedly, some put up false excuses and some sat away leaving me.
ai.seo_question: What was Imam Ali's assessment of the people's response to his call for help in Egypt?
ai.summary: In this address to Ibn Abbas, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contextualizes the martyrdom of Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr within the broader conquest of Egypt, elevating him as a model of loyal service and military prowess. He contrasts his own persistent, dual-mode exhortations (private and public) with the populace's fragmented response—ranging from reluctant compliance to false excuses and outright negligence—highlighting the political and social dynamics of the era. This passage underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the gap between leadership's clarity and the community's varied levels of commitment during the early Caliphate.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Egypt has, been conquered and Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr, may Allāh have mercy on him, has been martyred. We seek his reward from Allāh. He was a son who was a well-wisher, a hard worker, a sharp sword and a bastion of defence.

I had roused the people to join him and ordered them to reach him to help before this incident. I called to them secretly as well as openly repeatedly. Some of them came half-heartedly, some put up false excuses and some sat away leaving me.
